change: stages banded: 1 yama=B1; 2 niyama=B1; 3 āsana=B2; 4 prāṇāyāma=B2; 5 pratyāhāra=B3; 6 dhāraṇā=B3; 7 dhyāna=B3; 8 samādhi=B4
reason: Banded by what each limb is in the sūtra: restraints and observances are the ethical-purificatory foundation (B1); posture and breath preparatory discipline (B2); withdrawal, concentration and meditation one-pointedness (B3); samādhi as a limb is object-supported absorption (B4). Nothing in the eight limbs is itself B5+; YS 2.28 names viveka-khyāti as their fruit.
Same eight limb-names re-described in the Yoga Yājñavalkya (ten yamas and ten niyamas; prāṇāyāma with nāḍī-purification).
Tirumūlar's eightfold (aṭṭāṅka) yoga in Tamil uses the same eight limbs inside a Śaiva frame.
The Purāṇic eight limbs follow the Pātañjala order.
Haribhadra himself pairs his eight views with the eight limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreting the limbs inwardly.
Five limb-names shared (without yama, niyama, āsana; with tarka); older six-limbed scheme.
The Gheraṇḍa replaces yama/niyama with the six cleansing acts and adds mudrā; four limb-names shared.

change: stages banded: 1 savitarkā samāpatti=B4; 2 nirvitarkā samāpatti=B4; 3 savicārā samāpatti=B4; 4 nirvicārā samāpatti=B4; 5 sānanda=B4; 6 sāsmitā=B4; 7 adhyātma-prasāda, ṛtambharā prajñā, vive=B5; 8 asamprajñāta / nirbīja samādhi=B6; 9 dharmamegha samādhi=B6; 10 kaivalya=B7
reason: The samprajñāta coalescences and forms (vitarka→asmitā) are absorption with support (B4); truth-bearing insight and viveka-khyāti are the first direct seeing of the difference of puruṣa and sattva (B5); asamprajñāta/nirbīja and dharmamegha deepen that stilling (B6); kaivalya is final liberation (B7). Consistent with U10's pth:rajamartanda-samadhi-ladder and pth:yoga-sutra-kaivalya-sequence.
Bhoja's version of the same ladder (RM 1.17-18) with viveka-khyāti as a seventh samprajñāta rung.
Continuation of the top of this ladder in YS 4.25-34 (same dharmamegha → kaivalya segment).
Both are graded absorptions refining away coarser factors (vitarka/vicāra in both vocabularies); the Yoga Sūtra's goal (puruṣa's isolation) and the Buddhist cessation are not claimed to be the same.

change: stages banded: 1 śodhana through ṣaṭkarma=B1; 2 dṛḍhatā through āsana=B2; 3 sthiratā through mudrā=B2; 4 dhairya through pratyāhāra=B3; 5 lāghava through prāṇāyāma=B2; 6 pratyakṣa through dhyāna=B5; 7 nirliptatva through samādhi=B7
reason: Each means is banded by the fruit the text assigns it (1.11) and the kind of practice of its chapter: cleansing = purification (B1); posture and seals = preparatory discipline (B2); withdrawal = B3; breath = B2 (kept in the text's non-monotonic order); 'direct perception in the self' through meditation = B5; untaintedness and 'liberation without doubt' through samādhi = B7.
Stage 7 is expanded into six kinds of samādhi in GhS 7.
Four limb-names shared (āsana, pratyāhāra, prāṇāyāma, dhyāna, samādhi); yama/niyama replaced by bodily cleansing; mudrā added; order of prāṇāyāma and pratyāhāra reversed.

change: stages banded: 1 prāṇāyāma=B2; 2 pratyāhāra=B3; 3 dhyāna=B3; 4 dhāraṇā=B3; 5 tarka=B4; 6 samādhi=B4; 7 seeing the golden-hued maker=B5; 8 making all one in the imperishable=B7
reason: The six limbs are banded by kind (breath B2; withdrawal, meditation, concentration B3; tarka and samādhi B4); the vision of the golden-hued maker and of the self 'by the self' is the first seeing (B5); making all one in the imperishable, faults no longer clinging, is liberation (B7).
Same count of six and three shared limb-names (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, samādhi) in a different order, with anusmṛti for tarka; no historical claim is made here.
As above: six limbs with five shared names; Kālacakra has anusmṛti where the Maitrī has tarka.
Nātha six-limbed yoga (āsana instead of tarka).
Six-limbed yoga of the Yoga Upaniṣads.
The Amṛtanāda Upaniṣad's six limbs (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi) keep tarka as in the Maitrī.

change: stages banded: 1 mantrayoga=B2; 2 layayoga=B3; 3 haṭhayoga=B2; 4 rājayoga=B7
reason: Banded by the kind of each yoga: mantra repetition and haṭha technique are preparatory discipline (B2); laya is dissolution of mind by one-pointed indications (B3); rājayoga is the goal-state the text describes as liberating (B7). The grading is by adhikāra (P4), not a single ladder.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad repeats the same four yogas (it draws on the Dattātreyayogaśāstra).
Gorakṣa's Amaraughaprabodha names the same four yogas and grades them by practitioner.

change: stages banded: 1 ārambha=B2; 2 ghaṭa=B3; 3 paricaya=B4; 4 niṣpatti=B7
reason: Beginning = signs of breath-discipline (B2); ghaṭa = the conjunction of breaths and sense-withdrawal (B3); paricaya = breath and mind in the central channel with element-concentrations (B4); niṣpatti = rājayoga, samādhi of the one liberated while living (B7). Matches U29 (pth:siva-samhita-four-avasthas) and U04; U28 banded the HYP nāda version one band higher at the start (B3, B4, B4, B7), which reflects the HYP's own description.
The Haṭhayogapradīpikā's account of the same four stages through inner sound and the three knots.
The Śiva Saṃhitā's account of the same four stages.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad's account of the same four stages.
Both describe the breath/kuṇḍalinī passing the knots or centres up the central channel.

change: stages banded: 1 śubhecchā=B0; 2 vicāraṇā=B2; 3 tanumānasā=B3; 4 sattvāpatti=B5; 5 asaṃsakti=B6; 6 padārthābhāvanī=B6; 7 turyagā=B7; 8 turyātīta=B7
reason: Good desire is the turning (B0); inquiry through scripture and practice is preparatory (B2); thinning of mind is withdrawal from objects (B3); the mind resting in the self (the 'knower of Brahman') is the first direct seeing (B5); non-attachment and non-perception of objects deepen it (B6); turyagā is liberation while living (B7) and turyātīta bodiless liberation (B7).
The Varāha Upaniṣad gives the same seven stages (tanumānasī, padārthabhāvanā as variant spellings).
The Mahā Upaniṣad pairs these seven stages of knowledge with seven stages of ignorance.
Vidyāraṇya's Pañcadaśī 7 gives a different sevenfold series of the jīva's states (ignorance → satisfaction).
Graded knowers in the Yoga tradition (the bhāṣya's four kinds of yogin).

change: stages banded: 1 citta-śuddhi through karma and upāsanā=B1; 2 sādhana-catuṣṭaya=B0; 3 guru-upasatti=B0; 4 śravaṇa=B2; 5 manana=B2; 6 nididhyāsana=B4; 7 aparokṣa-jñāna=B5; 8 jīvanmukti=B7; 9 the liberated one's life for the world=B8; 10 videhamukti=B7
reason: Purifying rites are B1; the fourfold means and approaching the teacher are qualification/entry (B0, kept in the tradition's order after B1); hearing and reflection are scriptural study (B2); contemplation as a flow of like cognitions is absorption with support (B4); the immediate knowledge 'I am Brahman' is the first seeing (B5); jīvanmukti (B7) and videhamukti (B7) are liberation; the knower's life for others is B8.
Expands stage 6 (the auxiliaries of nididhyāsana: savikalpa and nirvikalpa samādhi).
Śaṅkara-attributed fifteen limbs of 'rāja-yoga' re-described as knowledge; a parallel Advaita path.
Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka uses the seven bhūmikās to grade Advaita knowers (stages 4-7 ~ this map's 7-9).
Dvaita also teaches śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsana leading to aparokṣa-jñāna, but of the Lord as other than the self; Dvaita rejects the identity this map's stage 7 names.

change: stages banded: 1 iruvinaiyoppu, malaparipāka, śaktinipāta=B0; 2 caryā=B2; 3 kriyā=B2; 4 yoga=B4; 5 jñāna=B5; 6 sāyujya / aṇaintu nirral=B7; 7 worship of the devotees and the temple=B8
reason: The descent of grace is the entry (B0); caryā and kriyā are devotional/ritual practice (B2); yoga is inner absorption on Śiva (B4); jñāna begins with the guru-given seeing of Śiva in the soul (B5); union is liberation (B7); the freed soul's worship of devotees and temple is activity after liberation (B8).
The Tamil ten acts (tacakāriyam) articulate the jñāna-pāda's culmination.
Both lead through devotional practice to a relational culmination (union as servant; prema) rather than identity.
Both end in liberation through knowledge given by grace/teaching; the Siddhānta rejects Advaita's identity of soul and Śiva (sāyujya is inseparability, not identity).

change: stages banded: 1 āṇavopāya=B2; 2 śāktopāya=B4; 3 śāmbhavopāya=B5; 4 anupāya=B7
reason: Āṇava works with supports of breath, body, image, letter and place (B2, rising to B3-B4); śākta is contemplation purifying thought, still with a conceptual object (B4); śāmbhava is thought-free immersion through the teacher's awakening — recognition (B5); anupāya is the recognition that nothing remains to be done (B7). Because the means are assigned by grade of grace (P4), the bands mark kind, not a required sequence.
Both hold that recognition of one's own nature can be immediate for some while others proceed by graded means; not claimed to be the same recognition.
Dzogchen and the Trika both speak of a means-less recognition; each tradition's account of what is recognized differs and neither endorses the equation.

change: stages banded: 1 bhakta=B0; 2 māheśvara=B1; 3 prasādī=B3; 4 prāṇaliṅgī=B5; 5 śaraṇa=B6; 6 aikya=B7
reason: Banded through the six kinds of devotion the tradition itself pairs with the sthalas: faith (B0), steadiness in vows (B1), attentiveness/serenity of mind (B3), experience — recognition of the liṅga as consciousness (B5), bliss of union (B6), equal flavour — oneness (B7).
The 101 sub-sthalas of the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi subdivide these six.
Both ascend by kinds of devotion (faith → steadiness → … → union / prema).

change: stages banded: 1 śraddhā=B0; 2 sādhu-saṅga=B0; 3 bhajana-kriyā=B2; 4 anartha-nivṛtti=B1; 5 niṣṭhā=B3; 6 ruci=B4; 7 āsakti=B4; 8 bhāva=B5; 9 prema=B7
reason: Faith and holy company are entry (B0); practice is devotional discipline (B2); removal of unwanted things is purification (B1, kept in textual order); steadiness is one-pointed constancy (B3); taste and attachment are absorption in the object of devotion (B4); bhāva, the first 'ray' of love and the start of perfection (bhāva-bhakti), is the first direct manifestation (B5); prema, the final goal, is banded at the culmination (B7). Same as U16's pth:madhurya-kadambini-stages.
Viśvanātha Cakravartin's Mādhurya-kādambinī expounds the same nine stages (subdividing practice and the anarthas); bands identical.
Continues stage 9: prema → sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga → anurāga → mahābhāva.
Nārada's aphorisms also lead from renunciation and company of the great to love.

change: stages banded: 1 mithyādṛṣṭi=unbanded; 2 sāsādana=unbanded; 3 samyag-mithyādṛṣṭi=B0; 4 avirata-samyagdṛṣṭi=B5; 5 deśavirata=B1; 6 pramatta-saṃyata=B1; 7 apramatta-saṃyata=B3; 8 apūrvakaraṇa=B4; 9 anivṛtti-bādara-sāmparāya=B6; 10 sūkṣma-sāmparāya=B6; 11 upaśānta-moha=B6; 12 kṣīṇa-moha=B6; 13 sayoga-kevalin=B7; 14 ayoga-kevalin=B7
reason: Stage 1 is the starting condition and 2 a stage of falling (unbanded); the mixed stage is the wavering threshold (B0); right view is the tradition's first real seeing (B5); vows are the ethical foundation (B1) — non-monotonic because the Jain path puts view before conduct (TS 1.1); careful restraint with virtuous meditation is B3; the first pure meditation with scriptural thought B4; the destruction/subsidence of passions B6; the omniscient states B7.
Umāsvāti's ten grades of karma-shedding (TS 9.45) run parallel to guṇasthānas 4-13.
Haribhadra's first four views fall within guṇasthāna 1; sthirā onward correspond to right view (4) and above; parā to kevala.
External self ~ guṇasthānas 1-3; internal self ~ 4-12; supreme self ~ 13-14 (Pūjyapāda's Samādhitantra).
The four pure meditations are distributed over guṇasthānas 8-14.

Right view (4) and stream-entry are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining rebirths; the Jain soul-doctrine and the Buddhist not-self teaching are not reconciled by this correspondence.

change: stages banded: 1 mitrā dṛṣṭi=B0; 2 tārā dṛṣṭi=B1; 3 balā dṛṣṭi=B2; 4 dīprā dṛṣṭi=B2; 5 sthirā dṛṣṭi=B5; 6 kāntā dṛṣṭi=B6; 7 prabhā dṛṣṭi=B6; 8 parā dṛṣṭi=B7
reason: Banded by the Jain criterion of view rather than by the paired Pātañjala limb where the two diverge: the sowing of the seeds of yoga (B0), observances (B1), steady posture and inner breath-control with hearing (B2), the breaking of the knot and right view in sthirā (B5), firm concentration and meditation with unattached activity (B6), absorption, omniscience and liberation in parā (B7).
Haribhadra pairs the views with Patañjali's limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreted inwardly; stated by the text itself.
The first four views lie within guṇasthāna 1 (ogha-dṛṣṭi); sthirā begins right view (4+); parā is kevala (13-14).
Haribhadra's four kinds of yogin grade the same practitioners by family and progress.

change: stages banded: 1 vikṣipta=unbanded; 2 yātāyāta=B3; 3 śliṣṭa=B4; 4 sulīna=B4; 5 unmanībhāva=B5
reason: The scattered mind is the starting condition (unbanded); the mind that goes and returns is beginning one-pointedness (B3); the clinging and dissolved minds are stable blissful absorption (B4); the no-mind state in which the self is realised is the first seeing (B5).
Graded minds/practitioners in the Yoga tradition; Vyāsa's five levels of mind (kṣipta … niruddha, YBh 1.1) are a closer analogue.
